text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Marshallian and Hicksian demands

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Marshallian and Hicksian demands stem from two ways of looking at the same problem- how to obtain the utility

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: we crave with the budget we have. Consumption duality expresses this problem as two sides of the same coin:

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: keeping our budget fixed and maximising utility (primal demand, which leads us to Marshallian demand curves) or

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: setting a target level of utility and minimising the cost associated with it (dual demand, which gives us Hicksian

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: demand curves). We must also look at the Lagrangian functions where we obtain the first derivatives.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Marshallian and Hicksian demand curvesThis leads us to the main difference between the two types of demand:

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Marshallian demand curves simply show the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: of it. Hicksian demand curves show the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded of it

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: assuming that the prices of other goods and our level of utility remain constant. This makes sense when we look

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: at consumption duality: for dual (Hicksian) demand, we maintain a fixed level of utility, and so our level of wealth,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: or income, must remain constant. We simply cannot be as satisfied if we do not maintain equal purchasing power.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Marshallian and Hicksian demand curves meet where the quantity demanded is equal for both sides of the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: consumer choice problem (maximising utility or minimising cost). For prices above this equilibrium point, consumer

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: wealth is higher with Hicksian demand curves than Marshallian demand curves, because to maintain utility

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: constant, Hicksian demand curves assume real wealth remains unchanged. Marshallian demand assumes only nominal

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: wealth remains equal. The opposite is true for prices below this point: Marshallian demand assumes that as

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: nominal wealth remains the same but price levels drop (negative inflation), the consumer is better off. Hicksian

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: demand assumes real wealth is constant, so the individual is worse off. This is why Marshallian demand curves are

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: more ‘stable’: they reflect both rent effect and substitution effect. Hicksian demand curves only show

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: substitution effects (utility is constant, therefore rent must remain constant), which means that demand varies

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: with price only because other options become more attractive.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Formally,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Marshallian demand (dX1) is a function of the price of X1, the price of X2 (assuming two goods) and the level of

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: income or wealth (m):

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: X*=dX1(PX1, PX2, m)

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Hicksian demand (hX1) is a function of the price of X1, the price of X2 (assuming two goods) and the level of

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: utility we opt for (U):

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: X*=hX1(PX1,PX2,U)

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: For an individual problem, these are obtained from the first order conditions (maximising the first derivatives) of

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: the Lagrangian for either a primal or dual demand problem.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Marshallian demand makes more sense when we look at goods or services that make up a large part of our

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: expenses. Here, the income effect is very large. However, for smaller purchases, we are willing to spend more or

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: less any amount as long as we derive the utility we expect to.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
